payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. Following an independent audit, the governing cycle-life figure is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge. The prototype’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. A projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.

Its measured gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, and projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte. An independent audit established 8,400 as the corrected, governing cycle-life figure; separately, its controlled accelerated-cycling test measured 4,800 cycles to the 80% capacity knee.
